concepts.name: Agents
concepts.explain: Agents are Markdown prompt files with YAML front matter: name, description, model list, tools and hooks. The product agents in extension/agents are templates; on activation the extension renders them (render.js fills in the runtime path and Python launcher) into a Copilot plugin folder, so only the three Frontier agents appear in the picker and the rest are personas they delegate to. The research arms in .github/agents are benchmark modes with pinned models and metrics hooks. Each agent's hooks run guard and context scripts from hooks/, and its instructions call tools such as lifecycle.py and loop.py. Persona agents (architects, engineers, testers, DevOps, data scientist, reviewers) are not written by hand: templates/personas/catalog.json lists each persona's kind (builder, designer or reviewer), goal, focus, skills and keywords, and personas.py renders them from the kind's template during extension/build.py. To add a persona, add it to the catalog and rebuild; to add any other agent, write extension/agents/hve-<name>.agent.md with its hooks, run extension/build.py and extend tests/test_extension.py.

concepts.name: Skills and loading
concepts.explain: Skills are folders with a SKILL.md (name and description in front matter) that agents load when a task matches. Library skills live in skills/admitted and are listed in skills/registry.json with categories and measured lift; plugin skills ship with the extension in plugins/harness-assist/skills and are always available. On every prompt the skill_loader hook ranks library skills with recommend.py, copies the relevant ones into .hve/skills for the session, flags a load over the guideline in skills/categories.json, and blocks reads of the others. context_load.py measures what skills, instructions and MCP tools add to every request.
questions: Why did a skill load or not load?
How do I add a plugin skill?
How big is the always-on context?

concepts.name: Skill evaluation and onboarding
concepts.explain: A skill enters the library only through a gate. scan.py checks a skill folder for security and structure problems; triage.py shortlists candidates per category; micro_eval.py and evaluate.py answer small tasks with and without the skill and have another model judge each pair blind; onboard.py admits the skill as provisional (static gate passed) or admitted (lift measured) and records it in skills/registry.json. The HVE skill-evaluator agent runs this in chat with the skill-judge and skill-worker personas; import_eval.py does the same for skills imported in bulk, and eval_skill.py runs paired benchmark sessions.

How is skill lift measured?

concepts.name: Expertise packs (plugins)
concepts.explain: An expertise pack is a plugin that carries one practice's knowledge: agents, skills, templates, a lifecycle, knowledge documents and rubrics, declared in hve-plugin.json (schema in schemas/). manifest.py validates a pack and measures each asset in tokens; plugin.py installs, enables and removes packs in the global store (~/.frontier-hve); store.py lists the packs a workspace can use; route.py decides which packs a request is about. When an ask starts, lifecycle_catalog.py routes the request to a pack lifecycle, ask_packs.py records the chosen packs and their token load in the contract, and stage_evidence.py checks a stage's evidence and rework. compose.py adds a pack's rubrics to the evaluation; packs.js installs packs in the editor and renders their agents.

concepts.name: Telemetry and metrics
concepts.explain: Telemetry has two sources. Hooks write what they see per session into .hve/runs/<session>: metrics.py joins tool-call events with token counts, agent_ledger.py records sub-agent starts and stops, and interventions.py logs every deny, block and stop. Copilot's own OpenTelemetry export (.hve/runs/copilot-otel.jsonl) carries tokens, cost and cache per chat call; the extension's research-telemetry command turns it on, otel_trim.py keeps it small and otel_prune.py archives it per benchmark run. trajectory.py, collect.py and provenance.py read both to show context growth, collect runs and prove which harness parts left evidence. Product agents do not run metrics.py, so per-call tokens are measured only in research runs or with OTel on.

concepts.name: Asks and delivery lifecycles
concepts.explain: An ask is one piece of work run through a delivery lifecycle. lifecycle.py picks a lifecycle (built in under templates/lifecycles, a workspace overlay or a pack) and writes the ask's contract.json: stages, skills, personas, packs, milestones and tasks. ask_plan.py renders plan.md with a sign-off checklist, and plan_check.py holds work until plan edits are synced back. During the ask lifecycle.py briefs sub-agents and tracks used skills and tasks; ask_report.py compares the contract with what happened and writes provenance.md. Frontier HVE Auto and Frontier HVE Collab drive this; environment.py records the harness, MCP servers and hooks the contract runs with.

What is in contract.json?
How is the provenance report built?

concepts.name: Verified feature loop
concepts.explain: Code is built one verified feature at a time. loop.py init locks feature_list.json with a shell check per feature and starts git; next picks the next failing feature; verify runs its check, commits on success, or records the attempt and asks diagnose.py which single fix rule applies, escalating to the human after repeated failures. loop_guard.py stops agents from editing the lock, marking features done themselves or pushing unverified work; guard_mode.json sets whether it enforces or advises. The engineer persona runs this loop for build stages.

concepts.name: Guards and hooks
concepts.explain: Hooks run before or after every tool call, prompt and sub-agent, as middleware between the model and the workspace. Policy guards deny or stop: module_guard.py blocks files over 500 lines, no_fallback.py rejects code that hides errors, error_guard.py pauses after a streak of failed commands, budget.py enforces a time budget, loop_guard.py protects loop state and flow_guard.py keeps creator-flow stages on their edges. guard_policy.py lets the user waive a guard after repeated trips. Context hooks add information: compaction.py tells sub-agents what to return, profile_detector.py learns user preferences, template_guard.py announces template policy. hve_paths.py locates .hve state for all of them.

concepts.name: Deliverable templates and backlog
concepts.explain: Documents such as a PRD, a technical design and a test strategy are created from versioned templates. manage.py resolves which template applies (bundled, configured, or from a pack), initializes the document with provenance markers and validates its sections; template_guard.py announces the policy and checks registered deliverables when a session stops. The product manager persona writes a PRD this way and turns it into a backlog that backlog.py validates against the PRD's requirements.

concepts.name: Output evaluation
concepts.explain: Finished work is judged before it is handed over. contract.py loads the evaluation contract (evaluation/frontier.eval.json: rubrics, validation hooks, council roles and thresholds); workflow.py scores each rubric with grounded evidence, runs the validation hooks that apply, and asks three reviewer roles (critical, balanced, coach) through the evaluation-reviewer agent; reflection.py is the CLI and makes the decision: pass, revise or human review. compose.py adds the rubrics of the expertise packs in use.

How do pack rubrics combine with the core rubrics?

concepts.name: VS Code extension
concepts.explain: The harness ships as one VSIX. build.py copies hooks/, tools/, skills and templates into extension/runtime and checks every runtime path the agent templates name; package.json declares the commands, settings and the Mission Control view. On activation extension.js registers Mission Control (extension/ui/: the Activity Bar sidebar and dashboard, which read .hve state and run only allowlisted lifecycle.py commands after a confirmation), finds Python, renders the agents (render.js) into a plugin folder registered with Copilot Chat, sets up the workspace's .hve folder, and offers telemetry and context-load commands; packs.js installs and manages expertise packs. Never edit extension/runtime: it is rebuilt from the sources.

Why does an agent show (Needs Python)?

concepts.name: Exports to other harnesses
concepts.explain: The same agents, skills and hooks run outside VS Code. export.py writes them for Copilot CLI, the Copilot cloud agent, Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, at user or project scope, with each client's file layout and hook format. agent_compat.py sits in front of every exported hook: it maps the client's hook payload to the VS Code shape the hooks read and maps the answer back. The export-harness skill walks a user through it, including the Azure DevOps MCP server.
questions: How do I use the agents in Claude Code?
Which hook events does each client support?

concepts.name: Git, PRs and parallel options
concepts.explain: Each verified feature gets its own stacked branch. branch_workflow.py records PRs and keeps a push queue that only branches the user ticks leave; parallel_options.py builds two or more approaches to one feature in separate git worktrees for the user to run and pick. The code-review, pr-push and parallel-options skills drive these steps in chat.
questions: When does a branch get pushed?
How do parallel options work?

concepts.name: Graph workflow (creator-flow)
concepts.explain: creator-flow runs work as a graph of stages (designer, prototyper, builder, architect, sweeper, grower, maintainer). flow.py is the state machine: a stage moves on only along a drawn edge, with deterministic evidence, and loops are capped. flow_guard.py stops a stage agent from finishing until it has moved the flow.
questions: How does a stage hand over?
What stops an endless loop?

concepts.name: Benchmarks and research
concepts.explain: The harness is tested against its own hypotheses. bench.py guides one benchmark session of a research arm, collect.py stores its output and metrics, blind.py prepares blind scoring behind random labels, and compare.py ranks modes and models by quality, then tokens, latency and cache. Findings and every design decision are written under research/.

concepts.name: Solution map
concepts.explain: The solution map lets people and agents understand a repository without reading it all. extract.py takes code facts from any repository (files, purposes, symbols, imports, mentions, agents, decisions); build.py places them in views and modules, adds concepts and data stores from docs/architecture/solution-map.config.json when present, and writes map.json, an overview and the explorer; solution_map.py answers explain, impact, search and status. The explorer shows the map as a force diagram, a tree or nested circles, filtered by concept, search or Cypher query.

conventions: extension/runtime/ is a build copy of hooks/, tools/, skills and templates made by extension/build.py: edit the sources, then rebuild.
Files stay under 500 lines (module_guard.py); fail fast with no fallbacks (no_fallback.py); one-line docstrings; type hints; the runtime stays Python 3.11 compatible.
Every design choice gets a decision (D-nnn) in research/decisions/decision_log.md and a tracker entry; only the user marks a tracker item validated.
Tests: python tests/test_<area>.py; extension: node --check extension/*.js; release: bump extension/package.json, build, package, install.
